formula: log(rt) ~ cond + (1 + cond | subj) + (1 + cond | item)
notes: Read E2_analysis.Rmd: brm(log(rt) ~ gram+int+gramxint + (1+gram+int+gramxint|subj) + (1+gram+int+gramxint|item)) on the critical-region words (pos == rcv) of target trials (expt == attraction) with 200 < rt < 8000. gram and int are sum contrasts of the four-level cond a-d, so the 2x2 is rendered as one four-level factor. The table is word-by-word; the subset is the paper's, not the table's. Practice survey filed the Experiment 2 reading-time model under its model 2.

formula: log(rt) ~ cond + (1 + cond | subj) + (1 + cond | item)
notes: Read the Experiment 3 analysis in the deposit scripts: brm(log(rt) ~ case+int+gram+casexint+casexgram+intxgram+casexintxgram + maximal subj and item slopes) on critical-region target words; case, int and gram are sum contrasts of the eight-level cond a-h, rendered here as one eight-level factor. formula: Accuracy ~ Type + (1 + Type | Participant) + (1 + Type | Item)
notes: Read the Experiment 1 script: brm(Accuracy ~ case+num+casexnum + (1+case+num+casexnum|Participant) + (1+case+num+casexnum|Item), bernoulli()) on target trials (Type a-d); case and num are sum contrasts of the four-level Type, rendered as one factor. Filler trials (Type f..) have no Item and are outside the model. Practice survey filed this under its model 1.

formula: log(RT) ~ Type + (1 + Type | Participant) + (1 + Type | Item)
notes: Same table and design as model 1; script fits brm(log(RT) ~ case+num+casexnum + maximal slopes) on correct target trials. Differs from model 1 in its response (RT, not Accuracy). Practice survey filed this under its model 2.

Paper's model is a dynamic structural equation model in Mplus (D ~ D_lag + G_lag + subculture + D_lag:subculture + G_lag:subculture + (1 + D_lag + G_lag | participant)). The lagged terms are not columns (lags of drbl and fem or masc within ID ordered by ts), so only the between-person term subculture (0 none, 1 jocks, 2 bears, 3 twinks, 4 fat gay men) and the participant grouping are rendered. drbl is state sexual desirability, the mean of des and att (script: dsbl = (des + att)/2); fem and masc are the two state gender responses, filed in ignore. RULE GAP: a model whose predictors are lags of columns can only be rendered on its non-lagged columns.

RESPONSE INFERRED: the paper models Hu scores (unbiased hit rates, arcsine transformed) hu_score ~ familiarity + (1 | participant) + (1 | voice_identity); the deposit holds only the trial-level raw data the Hu scores are computed from, so the trial-level Correct stands in for the response and label (PF, F, UF; VIG marks the keyboard trials) for familiarity. Voice identity is only inside the audio file name, not a column. Paper fits the Couples (n=27) and Controls groups separately (group, include filter). RULE GAP: a model on an aggregate whose aggregation input is the only table deposited.

RESPONSE INFERRED: the paper models Hu scores hu_score ~ familiarity * step + (1 | participant) (speaker identity dropped as it explained no variance); the deposit holds only the trial-level raw data, so Correct stands in for the Hu score, label for familiarity and mod_step (five levels) for the modulation step. Couples and Controls groups are fitted separately by the paper. RULE GAP: same as Task 1.

Columns match the paper's Task 3 binomial GLMM (correct ~ familiarity + (1 | participant) + (1 | voice identity)); the analysis plan gives the same specification with glmer(binomial). Trial-level table, familiarity PF versus UF. Couples and Controls groups fitted separately (group).

response_type categorical: object_present holds y, n and u (unknown) (merge correction). RESPONSE INFERRED: the paper's input models are lmer(PC ~ SibGroup + month + (1|subj)) on the per-infant monthly proportion of object-present utterances and lmer(Log.n ~ SibGroup + month + (1|subj)) on noun counts, both aggregated from this utterance-level table, which has no sibling column (SibGroup lives in SiblingsData.csv). The token-level object_present (y or n) with month is the finest table of the same model. Paper subsets audio_video == audio or video and caregiver type. RULE GAP: a model on an aggregate whose aggregation input is the deposited table.

Script: sibgroup.model <- lmerTest::lmer(Log.Totalwords ~ SibGroup + month + (1|subj), data=SiblingsData, REML=FALSE); Log.Totalwords is log(Total.words + 1) of the monthly CDI productive vocabulary. Binary and discrete sibling codings are the same structure with SibsYN or Siblings6 (filed in ignore). Infants without siblings carry a missing SibGroup if the loader reads the level None as NaN.

notes: Script BEHAV_fitModels.R fits approach.avoid ~ condition * RTc + (condition * RTc | ppid) with RTc the grand-mean-centred RT..s.; the raw RT..s. is used here (centring is linear). Paper keeps emotional trials only (Side.with.emotion != none), drops missed trials and RT <= 0.15 s. Experiment 2, 30 participants.
